title: I'm building a tool that turns game devlogs into videos, so I can focus on making games
author: Sudden_Network621
selftext:
I love building games. What I don't love is everything that comes after: making social media content, editing videos, writing posts, writing devlogs and constantly trying to get people interested in what I'm building.

So I started building **Devstory** for myself.

The idea is pretty simple. A little desktop companion called Nim observes your development process and automatically collects progress logs, screenshots, artwork, gameplay clips and turn them into a devlog. 

But the main goal isn't just writing devlogs.

**I want Devstory to turn those logs into engaging short documentary videos about the actual development journey.**

Not generic AI-generated promotional videos. Real stories about what you're building, what went wrong, what changed, and how your game evolved.

Ideally, you just develop your game and come back to find potential stories ready to turn into videos.

I'm also working on a website where developers can optionally publish their devlogs and showcase games that are still in development. Hopefully, that gives people another way to discover interesting indie projects.

It's still an early prototype, and the automated video pipeline isn't finished yet. I made this trailer to show where I want to take it.

**I'm curious about two things:**

1. Do you struggle with promoting your games as much as I do?
2. Would you actually use something that turns your development progress into ready-to-post videos?

I'm building this because I genuinely want to spend more time making games and less time marketing them. Curious whether other indie devs feel the same.

replies.author: Sudden_Network621

I would be happy when you would test it and give me direct and honest feedback. What system do you have mac or windows?

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body: I feel like the very, very last thing this sub needs is a way to automate the production of the 'this is my journey' linkedin posts

replies.author: Sudden_Network621
replies.body: I do think its really interesting to follow an indie game devs journey, it gives personality and you root more for them. There are different taste of course, but in my opinion I would love to see behind the scenes and how the journey goes on until the game is published 😊

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
I like to see that too, but the 'this is my journey' linkedin posts made here aren't that. they're just ChatGPT written ad copy 

The proposed application here just industrializes the creation of that ad copy

replies.author: Sudden_Network621
replies.body:
I actually agree with you on that. I don’t want more generic AI written LinkedIn posts either.

The whole reason I’m building this is because I enjoy following the actual development journey, including the struggles, failed attempts, weird decisions and little breakthroughs.

The idea is to capture what really happened while developing, preserve the original artwork and gameplay, and use that to create short documentary style videos. Not invent some inspirational founder story or turn everything into an ad.

And if nothing interesting happened that day, there’s no reason to force a post. That’s also why I’m testing this publicly. I want to find out whether AI can genuinely help tell those stories without making everything feel artificial.
